clue.text: Moss Bros arranged 25% off everything — Queen pops in for a hat

indicators.note: the monarch's cipher pops in among the rearranged letters
the letters left from the shop name are arranged in a new order
a sale slogan read literally: the stated share is knocked off the whole shop name

parts.note: a quarter of eight letters is two, here the fourth letter of each word
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the cipher of the late Queen

explanation.surface: A sale at the menswear chain: a quarter off everything, and the Queen drops in to buy a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Moss Bros is a British menswear and suit-hire chain. '25% off everything' knocks off the fourth letter of each word, leaving MOS BRO, which 'arranged' scrambles; the Queen's cipher then 'pops in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sombrero is a broad-brimmed Mexican headwear, one specific kind of the general category.

clue.text: Old revue adapted to make artistic work

indicators.note: a stage show that is adapted is reworked, so its letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: An old stage revue reworked into a new piece of art.
explanation.definitionFit: Oeuvre is the French-derived term for a creator's body of output, or a single piece of it.

clue.text: Only child has this revolutionary American browser

indicators.note: something that revolves turns round, so the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: an only child has no sibling: NO SIB

explanation.surface: An only child with a revolutionary American web browser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns NO SIB round. 'browser' is not software but an animal that browses, nibbling vegetation.
explanation.definitionFit: The bison of the North American plains grazes and browses on grass and shrubs, hence a browser.

clue.text: Male pride damaged on the surface

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Male pride is damaged, but only superficially.
explanation.definitionFit: Epidermal relates to the epidermis, the outer layer of skin, so it describes the surface.

clue.text: Cut too much perhaps when supervised

definitions.meaning: read as ..., to saw too far or too much

explanation.surface: Someone who was overseeing a job ended up cutting too much.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is an invented word, over plus saw, so 'perhaps' flags it.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise; the past tense matches the clue's past participle-like verb.

clue.text: After month, act to cut nails

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first in the answer

parts.note: DEC is short for December
an act of parliament is a law

explanation.surface: After a month, someone acts to have their nails cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To declaw an animal is to remove its claws, a surgical trimming of its nails.

clue.text: Department head's beginning to show intensity of feeling?

indicators.note: beginning means the first letter of the word head is taken

explanation.surface: A department head starting to show strong emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Depth can mean profundity or strength of emotion, as in the depth of her grief; the question mark marks this looser sense.

clue.text: Chapter rendered up-to-date — it involves dramatic change in order

indicators.note: rendered here means made over or translated into a new form, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A chapter is revised to bring it up to date, involving dramatic changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rendered' rearranges UPTODATE into OUPDETAT. 'order' is the political order, the regime.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup d'état is the sudden overthrow of a government, a violent shift in the ruling regime.

clue.text: Approval accomplished with little resistance

parts.note: amen expresses assent or approval
an accomplished person is able, skilled

explanation.surface: Approval was won without much of a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone amenable is compliant and open to persuasion, offering little opposition.

clue.text: Cereal succeeded in upsetting part of digestive system

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the reversed body part
in a down clue upsetting turns over, here in an across one it simply reverses the word

parts.note: the ileum is the last section of the small intestine
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A breakfast cereal that upsets someone's gut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' reverses ILEUM to MUELI, and S goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a breakfast mix of oats, nuts and dried fruit, so a type of cereal.

clue.text: Recommends online brides?

definitions.meaning: to espouse a cause is to advocate or support it
read as ..., spouses found on the internet, e- meaning electronic

explanation.surface: Someone advocates finding a wife on the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: Espousing an idea means championing it; the playful second reading treats the e- prefix as internet-based.

clue.text: Royal bride in California's beginning to get covered by newspapers

indicators.note: the inner pieces are covered, enclosed, by the word for newspapers

parts.note: the press is newspapers collectively

indicators.note: the opening letter of the state name is taken

explanation.surface: A royal bride in California starts to be followed by the papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bride' is a link-like flourish of the surface: the definition is Royal alone, as the clue reads 'Royal bride' to suggest Meghan Markle.
explanation.definitionFit: A princess is a female member of a royal family, so a royal is a fair general term.

clue.text: Renovate most of home, and he'll provide the raw materials

indicators.note: to renovate is to do up, so these letters are made over in a new order
most of the word home means it loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A builder's labourer is told to renovate most of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims HOME to HOM; 'Renovate' rearranges HOM and AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A hodman is a builder's labourer who carries bricks and mortar in a hod to the bricklayers.

clue.text: Measure archer's speed? You need to take the long view

definitions.meaning: read as TIME WILL(IAM) TELL: clock the speed of the legendary Swiss archer

definitions.text: You need to take the long view
definitions.meaning: the saying means only the future will show the truth

explanation.surface: Clock the archer's speed: you need a long-term outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: William Tell is the Swiss folk hero who shot an apple from his son's head; 'Will' is his short name.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb counsels patience: the outcome becomes clear only with the passing of months or years.

clue.text: Follow legal case that's put on for training purposes

parts.note: to track someone is to follow them
a suit is a lawsuit, a legal action

explanation.surface: Follow a court case that has been staged for training.
explanation.definitionFit: A tracksuit is the loose garment athletes wear while exercising, so it is worn for workouts.

clue.text: Does one take interest in predating customer base?

definitions.text: Does one take interest in predating customer base?

parts.words: Does one take interest in predating customer base?
parts.note: interest is charged on a loan, and predating suggests preying on borrowers like a predator in the sea

explanation.surface: A business seemingly curious about a history earlier than its clients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'predating' looks like coming earlier in time but means preying on; 'interest' is the money charged, not curiosity.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a lender who charges extortionate rates of payment, preying on desperate borrowers.

clue.text: It's anticlimactic as nobody lets off steam

parts.note: none means not one person
to vent is to release pent-up feelings or gas

explanation.surface: A disappointing occasion where nobody blows off steam.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-event is an occasion that fails to live up to expectations, a disappointing let-down.

clue.text: Save lamb to roast, eating starters for family events for Easter?

indicators.note: the cooked mixture eats, takes in, the initial letters
food that is roasted is transformed by cooking, so these letters are recast

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: starters are the first letters of the two following words

explanation.surface: Cooking lamb for family gatherings at Easter, with starters served first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roast' rearranges SAVE LAMB and TO; 'eating' sets the first letters of family and events inside that mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is a church festival whose date changes each year, the classic example of a movable feast.

clue.text: Double blow for supporters

parts.note: to fan is to blow air gently
Double asks for a second word meaning blow: a club is a heavy blow, as a verb to strike

explanation.surface: A double punch landed on behalf of the fans.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces mean blow, one gentle and one violent, and 'Double' says to use the word twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan club is an organised group of admirers of a celebrity or team.

clue.text: English spar, showing wit

parts.note: a sprit is a small spar crossing a sail diagonally

explanation.surface: An English sparring match showing wit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spar' looks like boxing but is the nautical pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is French-derived for liveliness of mind, quick cleverness.

clue.text: Vessel of ale containing a third of keg

indicators.note: the word for ale holds the other two pieces

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

indicators.note: a third of a three-letter word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A glass of ale holding a third of the keg.
explanation.definitionFit: A beaker is a drinking cup or laboratory glass, a container for liquid.

clue.text: Values carpets

definitions.meaning: to carpet someone is to reprimand them, and to rate is an old word for scolding

explanation.surface: Assessing the worth of floor coverings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carpets' is a verb: to haul someone over the coals.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are verbs: to rate is to appraise, and in older use to berate.

clue.text: Merry session around east end of London's curiosity

indicators.note: the jumbled letters wrap around the single letter
a merry, tipsy session is jumbled up, so its letters are rearranged
the east, right-hand, end of the word London is its final letter

explanation.surface: A boozy session in London's East End arouses curiosity.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the London district, but here it is the last letter. 'Merry' scrambles SESSION, which goes 'around' N.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosiness is prying inquisitiveness about other people's affairs.

clue.text: What Americana! Velvet trousers, cut-off cords (one of them)

indicators.note: used as a verb: the phrase pockets, trousers, the answer within it

explanation.surface: Americana fashion: velvet trousers and cut-off cord shorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cords' are corduroy trousers on the surface but umbilical cords in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The belly button is where the umbilical cord was cut off, so each of us has one.

clue.text: One subject to ridicule trapped in genuine contradiction

indicators.note: this phrase puts the target of mockery inside the word for genuine

parts.note: real means genuine
the butt of a joke is the one mocked

explanation.surface: A mocked person caught in a real contradiction.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal is a counter-argument refuting a claim.

clue.text: What's commercial TV read out?

indicators.note: out means not in order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about what commercial television reads out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read out' looks like a homophone signal, but 'out' alone scrambles TV READ.
explanation.definitionFit: An advert is a commercial, a paid advertisement on television.

clue.text: Standing stone American tours regularly

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word tours

explanation.surface: A standing stone visited regularly by American tourists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing stone' reads as a menhir, but 'Standing' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is someone's position or rank in society, their social standing.

clue.text: Synthetic material to make e.g. cakes low in calories

parts.note: you bake cakes
lite is a marketing spelling of light, meaning low-calorie

explanation.surface: A synthetic substance for producing diet cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Bakelite is an early plastic, a phenol-formaldehyde resin used for old telephones and radios.
